key_insight: A hybrid translator combines deterministic compilation with LLM agents to convert quantum MLIR dialects into QIR, using independent simulators to check output agreement.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce dialect-specific compiler work for quantum software interoperability, though the abstract reports no materials-science application.
method: Use deterministic translation for Catalyst and Quake, and LLM agents for unseen dialects or failed-output repair.
Execute source MLIR and generated QIR on independent simulators and compare distributions using total variation distance (TVD).
Support smaller open-weight models with inline context and a guardrail assembler that reconstructs valid QIR from incomplete output.
evidence_signal: Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1–100 qubits, deterministic translation was gate-exact on all 70 evaluated circuit–dialect pairs with average similarity (1−TVD) above 95%; four of six models generated valid logical-level QIR for an unseen FTQC dialect on the first iteration.
watch_item: Valid QIR does not by itself establish semantic equivalence; unseen-dialect translation still requires behavioral validation.
paper_title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
